newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P rates St George Bank A/A-1.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P rates St George Bank A/A-1.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Wednesday it had assigned an "A" long term counterparty rating and "A-1" short term rating to St George Bank Ltd upon the completion of its acquisition of Advance Bank Ltd in early 1997.

S&P said it expected to assign a stable outlook to the merged bank but until the merger was finalised, St George would keep its current ratings of A/A-2 and remain under credit watch with positive implications.

"The merger should provide St George with greater flexibility to withstand competitive pressures which continue to build in the Australian banking industry. The main benefits of the merger will be in market position and geographic diversity," S&P said in a statement.
The profitability of the merged banks would be slightly above that of St George on its own in the medium term, S&P said.

S&P said goodwill amortisation would be high as a result of the large premium by St George and would initially offset much of the cost savings which St George estimated at A$140 million a year over three years.
"Nevertheless, profitability levels will be competitive and are also expected to strengthen with further contributions from fee income," S&P said.
S&P said it would monitor both the ongoing progress of the bank, once the merger was completed and its success at fully integrating the banks and achieving the benefits.
